text: Compared with the earlier promise, the apparent difference is narrowed. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and in Genesis 22 that promise concerning Isaac is turned into a test. The action rests on one Hebrew word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham utters three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel. It is the same word, yet in each utterance its meaning is altered, and each utterance costs Abraham more.
